task.description: WF-02 Step 2c -- security gate on ELIXIR-DEV's Step 2a implementation of REQ-074 (group/group-membership routes, new group_members join table).
acceptance_criteria: Every applicable invariant (INV-1..INV-8) assessed against the actual diff and PASSes
Cross-tenant-join failure mode specifically verified (add_group_member/3, list_group_members/3, delete_group/2's not-exists subquery)

result.summary:
Reviewed git diff main...HEAD for feature/WF02-REQ074-20260822 (commit 4a0af45). Scope test: diff adds two migrations (priv/repo/migrations/20260822000101 and _000102), a new Ecto schema (lib/letflow/identity/group_member.ex), a new changeset (group.ex create_changeset/2), six new Identity context functions, six new routes, and two pre-existing-regression fixes -- this is squarely a tenant-data path (new join table linking two tenant-scoped entities). All eight invariants assessed:

INV-1 (APPLIES, PASS) -- the load-bearing one. add_group_member/3 (identity.ex:381-394) does Repo.get(Group, group_id, prefix: prefix) then Repo.get(User, user_id, prefix: prefix), both scoped, BEFORE any insert; insert_or_fetch_group_member/3 only runs after both succeed. This is structural, not a runtime check: prefix selects a distinct Postgres schema, so a user_id belonging to tenant B's own schema simply has no row under tenant A's prefix -- Repo.get returns nil the same way a globally-nonexistent id would, by construction of schema-per-tenant, not by any comparison of tenant ids. Read the cross-tenant test directly (test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs:759-784): it provisions two real tenants, inserts a user only in tenant B, POSTs to tenant A's add-member route with that user's id, asserts byte-identical 404 vs a genuinely nonexistent uuid, AND asserts Repo.aggregate(GroupMember, :count, prefix: tenant_a.schema_name) == 0 -- a real DB-level row-count check, not vacuous. list_group_members/3 (identity.ex:479-505): single Repo.all(query, prefix: prefix) call over a query joining GroupMember to User on user_id -- Ecto's prefix: option applies uniformly to every unprefixed source table in the query, so both sides of the join resolve inside the same tenant schema; there is no separate per-source prefix to independently misconfigure here (both Group/GroupMember/User schemas carry no @schema_prefix override), so a mismatched-scope join is not structurally possible under this pattern. delete_group/2 (identity.ex:435-449): read the actual query -- from(g in Group, as: :group, where: g.id == ^id, where: not exists(from m in GroupMember, where: parent_as(:group).id == m.group_id)), executed via Repo.delete_all(query, prefix: prefix). Re-verified ELIXIR-DEV's to_sql claim independently by tracing Ecto's documented behavior: Repo.delete_all/2's prefix: option is applied by Ecto's planner to every table reference in the full query AST (outer query and every subquery alike) unless a source explicitly names its own prefix -- neither Group nor GroupMember does, so the not-exists subquery necessarily resolves group_members inside the same schema as the outer groups reference. No cross-tenant leak vector (a tenant-A delete cannot be blocked by tenant-B's members, nor vice versa). Two new migrations (both read directly): both guard with `if prefix() do`, both prefix every create/alter/index call, matching the established convention exactly.

INV-2 -- NOT APPLICABLE (S4 API-authorization semantics not the concern here; response shaping checked under the INV-2-equivalent note below anyway). INV-3 -- NOT APPLICABLE (S5 not started). INV-4 (APPLIES, PASS) -- no new secret-resolving code in this diff; grep for System.get_env/hardcoded-secret patterns shows no new hits in the changed files. INV-5 -- NOT APPLICABLE formally (S4 lookup-by-ID not yet the named stage) but the cross-tenant test above already demonstrates byte-identical 404/not-found indistinguishability as a matter of fact for this diff's own add-member and list-group-members paths, so no gap exists in practice either. INV-6 (APPLIES, PASS) -- this handoff itself is the proof-of-scoping artifact; each new data-access path's scoping mechanism is stated above. INV-7 (APPLIES, PASS) -- grep for Repo.query across lib/ and priv/repo/migrations/ shows zero new hits in the REQ-074 diff (the four pre-existing hits in sandbox_pool.ex/sandbox_pool/fixture_loader.ex/tenant_provisioning.ex predate this change and use bound params or server-generated schema-name identifiers, not tenant-controlled data); every new query is Ecto.Query/Ecto.Schema based. INV-8 (APPLIES, PASS) -- grep for the bare `{:ok, X} = ...` pattern in the changed files shows one hit relevant to this diff (routers/identity.ex:453, `{:ok, %{groups: groups, total: total}} = Identity.list_groups(opts)`); list_groups/1's own @spec and body guarantee it always returns `{:ok, _}` (no error path exists), matching this codebase's existing precedent for that exact idiom elsewhere in the same router (e.g. line 209). Not a crash risk on realistic input.

Group_map/1 (routers/identity.ex:599-614) is a hand-built 5-key map, not a Jason.Encoder derivation -- matches REQ-073's user_map/1 discipline exactly, same file.

The two pre-existing-regression fixes independently re-verified: (1) identity_migration.ex's copy_groups/2 (lines 141-151) -- narrowed select: struct(g, [:id, :name, :inserted_at, :updated_at]) is exactly the four columns the legacy public.groups table has (confirmed against the migration history comment and the fix's own inline rationale); it does not drop any column that used to migrate correctly -- the two new columns (display_name/description) never existed on the legacy source table in the first place, so there was nothing to preserve for them, and the destination schema's nullable columns correctly default to nil for migrated legacy rows. No INV-1/INV-7 property of this cutover path changed -- the WHERE-clause tenant scoping (fragment on g.tenant_id) is untouched. (2) The migration renumbering (20260822000001/2 -> 20260822000101/2, avoiding collision with test/letflow/api/context_test.exs's hardcoded @probe_migration_version) is a pure filename/manifest-registration change with no security surface.

Scope check (point 8): git diff main...HEAD --stat confirms the changed-file set is exactly what's expected -- identity module/schema/migration files, router, tenant_provisioning manifest, identity_migration.ex (the documented regression fix), test file, design doc, and bookkeeping (handoffs/registry/docs/anti-patterns/requirements status). Nothing under lib/letflow/plugs/*.ex or lib/letflow/api/context.ex / authorization.ex -- matches the design's own conclusion that no authorization change was needed for this requirement.

Verdict: PASS. Route to REVIEWER per WF-02 Step 2d for the two explicitly-preserved open questions (OQ-1, OQ-3) and general OTP-idiom/scope-creep review.

issues.description: priv/repo/migrations/20260822000102_create_group_members_tenant_scoped.exs uses on_delete: :nothing on both group_members FKs (group_id, user_id). This is a deliberate, documented tradeoff (migration's own header comment): delete_group/2 refuses deletion of a non-empty group at the application layer, so the group_id FK's on_delete clause is never really exercised against a non-empty group. However, no equivalent applicgation-layer guard exists yet for deleting a USER who still has group memberships -- if a future user-deletion path is added without an equivalent not-exists guard (or without accompanying application-level cleanup of that user's group_members rows), on_delete: :nothing would leave orphaned group_members rows referencing a deleted user_id, which list_group_members/3's join would then silently exclude (INNER JOIN to a nonexistent user just drops the row) rather than error -- not a cross-tenant leak, but a data-integrity gap worth flagging now before it's forgotten. Not a blocker for REQ-074 itself: this requirement does not add or change any user-deletion path, and the current design's only mutation of group_members membership is add/remove-by-group, both of which correctly clean up their own rows. Recommend a follow-up issue tracking this for whichever future requirement adds hard user deletion.
